# FrameWorks

> Open live video platform with managed hybrid edges. MCP-native with wallet auth and x402 payments.

## Product

- [FrameWorks](https://frameworks.network/): Live streaming SaaS with customer-operated MistServer/Helmsman edge capacity attached to the FrameWorks-operated Foghorn, federation, storage, DNS/TLS, billing, analytics, and control plane.
- [Showcase](https://frameworks.network/showcase): What ships today, what is up next, and what is further out, generated from the same feature registry as the docs feature matrix.
- [Stream test](https://frameworks.network/stream-test): Play an HLS, DASH, WHEP, or MistServer stream in the browser, or publish to a WHIP endpoint with StreamCrafter.
- [Network explorer](https://frameworks.network/network): Public map of FrameWorks infrastructure and the Livepeer orchestrators that transcode its streams, with regional prices and performance.
- [Pricing](https://frameworks.network/pricing): Beta pricing for the hosted Free tier, Supporter, Developer, Production, pay-as-you-go, and Enterprise.
- [About](https://frameworks.network/about): Mission, architecture, and history of FrameWorks and the MistServer team behind it.
- [Contact](https://frameworks.network/contact): Reach the video engineers for projects, trial usage, custom pricing, or a shared Slack or WhatsApp channel.
- [Documentation](https://logbook.frameworks.network/): Operator and builder docs for streams, self-hosting, routing, billing, agent access, and migration workflows.

## Docs

- [MCP Integration](https://logbook.frameworks.network/agents/mcp): Resources, tools, prompts, x402 payments
- [Skill File](https://frameworks.network/SKILL.md): Agent quick-start guide
- [Agent Overview](https://logbook.frameworks.network/agents/overview): Discovery, auth, and capabilities
- [Skipper Video Consultant](https://logbook.frameworks.network/agents/skipper): RAG-grounded streaming expertise
- [Go live from your browser](https://logbook.frameworks.network/builders/go-live-browser): Stream from the dashboard with StreamCrafter, with your camera, screen share, and layouts in one browser tab and no encoder to install
- [StreamCrafter](https://logbook.frameworks.network/builders/ingest): Browser publishing over WHIP from cameras, screen shares, and media files, with scenes, layers, overlays, transitions, and audio mixing. React, Svelte, Web Components, and vanilla packages. Beta: the SDK will change substantially as cloud production arrives
- [Multistreaming](https://logbook.frameworks.network/builders/multistreaming): Native MistServer push from the origin node to Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook, X, and custom RTMP, RTMPS, or SRT destinations, with per-destination status and errors
- [Feature matrix](https://logbook.frameworks.network/platform/feature-matrix): Every platform feature with its status, generated from the feature registry
- [Roadmap](https://logbook.frameworks.network/roadmap): Planned work by area, marked Now, Next, or Later

## Migrating

FrameWorks is an alternative to managed video APIs like Mux, Bunny Stream, and Livepeer Studio. It runs as hosted SaaS, with customer-operated edges attached to the FrameWorks platform, or fully self-hosted as an independent platform (public domain, deployed with the `frameworks` CLI). Federating a self-hosted platform with the FrameWorks network is not supported.

- [Migration overview](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate): Pick your starting point
- [Migrate from Mux](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/mux): REST → GraphQL, signed playback, simulcast, recordings
- [Migrate from Livepeer Studio](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/livepeer-studio): API shape and access-control differences
- [Migrate from Bunny Stream](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/bunny-stream): VOD carries over, live capabilities open up
- [Migrate from MistServer](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/mistserver): Add a control plane, or federate edge capacity
- [Migrate from Castr](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/castr): Live streams, destinations, embeds, and recordings, with what is up next
- [Migrate from Flussonic](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/flussonic): Keep your hardware as FrameWorks edges, self-host the full stack, or move to the hosted platform
- [Migrate from any video API](https://logbook.frameworks.network/migrate/generic): The universal checklist

## API

- MCP Discovery: https://bridge.frameworks.network/.well-known/mcp.json
- MCP Endpoint: POST https://bridge.frameworks.network/mcp (streamable-http)
- GraphQL: POST https://bridge.frameworks.network/graphql
- [GraphQL schema reference](https://logbook.frameworks.network/builders/api-schema/): Public operations, arguments, types, and deprecations
- [SDKs](https://logbook.frameworks.network/builders/sdks/): Typed TypeScript, Go, and Python operations
- Wallet Login: GraphQL mutation walletLogin at https://bridge.frameworks.network/graphql

## Auth

- Bearer token (JWT or API key)
- Wallet signature (EIP-191 personal_sign)
- x402 (gasless USDC on Base/Arbitrum)

## Self-Hosted Edge Infrastructure

- Cluster marketplace: discover and subscribe to regional clusters via MCP (browse_marketplace, subscribe_to_cluster)
- Edge clusters: create_edge_cluster returns enrollment token and Foghorn address for edge provisioning
- Edge provisioning: `frameworks edge provision --enrollment-token <token> --ssh user@host`
- Peering: preferred ↔ official clusters always peered; other subscribed clusters peer on demand when streams trigger it
- Node lifecycle: frameworks edge mode (draining/maintenance/normal), frameworks edge doctor, frameworks edge logs
- Node management via API (no SSH): set_node_mode, get_node_health (Gateway → Commodore → Foghorn)
- MCP tools: create_enrollment_token, get_node_info, manage_node, set_node_mode, get_node_health
